question: How many customers are there?
sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS customer_count FROM customers;
note: Agent SQL from eval/results/harvest.json (h01). Counts customer_id rows (one per order), not people.

question: How many customers live in the state of Minas Gerais (MG)?
sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS mg_customers FROM customers WHERE customer_state = 'MG';
note: Agent SQL from eval/results/harvest.json (h02). Counts customer_id rows (one per order), not people.

question: How many customers have placed more than one order?
sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS customers_with_more_than_one_order FROM ( SELECT customer_id FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 1 ) AS t;
note: Agent SQL from eval/results/harvest.json (h03). Groups by customer_id, which has exactly one order each, so the answer is 0.

question: Which 3 cities have the most customers? Give each city and its number of customers, from most to least.
sql: SELECT customer_city, COUNT(*) AS customer_count FROM customers WHERE customer_city IS NOT NULL AND customer_city <> '' GROUP BY customer_city ORDER BY customer_count DESC, customer_city ASC LIMIT 3;
note: Agent SQL from eval/results/harvest.json (h04). Counts customer_id rows per city, not people.

question: What is the total of all payments (payment_value) for orders that contain at least one product from the 'beleza_saude' category, whatever the order status?
sql: SELECT COALESCE(SUM(op.payment_value), 0) AS total_payment_value FROM order_payments op JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = op.order_id WHERE EXISTS ( SELECT 1 FROM order_items oi JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE oi.order_id = o.order_id AND p.product_category_name = 'beleza_saude' );
note: Agent SQL from eval/results/harvest.json (h05). Picks the orders with EXISTS before summing payments: no fan-out.

question: Across all orders, what are the total freight value of the items and the total amount paid? Give both numbers.
sql: SELECT COALESCE((SELECT SUM(oi.freight_value) FROM order_items oi), 0) AS total_freight_value, COALESCE((SELECT SUM(op.payment_value) FROM order_payments op), 0) AS total_payment_value;
note: Agent SQL from eval/results/harvest.json (h06). Two separate scalar subqueries: no join, no fan-out.

question: What is the average review score of orders that include at least one product from the 'cama_mesa_banho' category? Round to two decimals.
sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(ro.review_score), 2) AS average_review_score FROM orders o JOIN order_reviews ro ON ro.order_id = o.order_id WHERE EXISTS ( SELECT 1 FROM order_items oi JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE oi.order_id = o.order_id AND p.product_category_name = 'cama_mesa_banho' );
note: Agent SQL from eval/results/harvest.json (h07). Picks the orders with EXISTS; joining orders to reviews keeps one row per review.

question: What is the average total amount paid per order? Round to two decimals.
sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(total_per_order), 2) AS avg_total_paid_per_order FROM ( SELECT order_id, SUM(payment_value) AS total_per_order FROM order_payments GROUP BY order_id) AS t;
note: Agent SQL from eval/results/harvest.json (h08). Sums payments per order before averaging: right grain.

question: How many orders include at least one product from the 'esporte_lazer' category?
sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT oi.order_id) AS orders_with_sport FROM order_items oi JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE p.product_category_name = 'esporte_lazer';
note: Agent SQL from eval/results/harvest.json (h09). Looks risky (join with order_items) but counts DISTINCT order_id: right grain.

question: How many orders include at least one item from a seller located in the state of Rio de Janeiro (RJ)?
sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT oi.order_id) AS orders_with_RJ_seller FROM order_items oi JOIN sellers s ON oi.seller_id = s.seller_id WHERE s.seller_state = 'RJ';
note: Agent SQL from eval/results/harvest.json (h10). Looks risky (join with order_items) but counts DISTINCT order_id: right grain.

question: How many reviews have a score of 1?
sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_reviews_with_score_1 FROM order_reviews WHERE review_score = 1;
note: Agent SQL from eval/results/harvest.json (h11). Counts order_reviews rows; the same review_id can cover several orders. Correct: count(DISTINCT review_id).

question: How many orders were delivered to the customer in 2017?
sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS delivered_orders_2017 FROM orders WHERE order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL AND EXTRACT(year FROM order_delivered_customer_date) = 2017;
note: Agent SQL from eval/results/harvest.json (h12). Filters by delivery date, as the question asks.

question: In which month of 2017 (as a number from 1 to 12) were the most orders delivered to customers, and how many?
sql: SELECT EXTRACT(MONTH FROM order_delivered_customer_date) AS month, COUNT(*) AS delivered_orders FROM orders WHERE order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL AND DATE_PART('year', order_delivered_customer_date) = 2017 GROUP BY month ORDER BY delivered_orders DESC, month ASC LIMIT 1;
note: Agent SQL from eval/results/harvest.json (h13). Filters and groups by delivery date, as the question asks.

question: How many orders were approved in January 2018?
sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS approved_orders_jan2018 FROM orders WHERE order_status = 'approved' AND order_approved_at >= '2018-01-01'::timestamp AND order_approved_at < '2018-02-01'::timestamp;
note: Agent SQL from eval/results/harvest.json (h14). Reads 'approved' as the current order_status instead of the approval date, so the count is 0. No named trap: next_step has to catch it.

question: How many orders were there in the first quarter of 2018?
sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS orders_q1_2018 FROM orders WHERE order_purchase_timestamp >= TIMESTAMP '2018-01-01 00:00:00' AND order_purchase_timestamp < TIMESTAMP '2018-04-01 00:00:00';
note: Agent SQL from eval/results/harvest.json (h15). No date named: purchase date, per the convention.

question: How many items from the 'informatica_acessorios' category were sold?
sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS sold_items FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE p.product_category_name = 'informatica_acessorios' AND o.order_status = 'delivered';
note: Agent SQL from eval/results/harvest.json (h16). Delivered orders only, as the sales convention requires.

question: What was the total sales revenue in 2017, counting item prices only (without freight)?
sql: SELECT COALESCE(SUM(oi.price), 0) AS total_revenue_2017 FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE o.order_purchase_timestamp >= TIMESTAMP '2017-01-01 00:00:00' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < TIMESTAMP '2018-01-01 00:00:00';
note: Agent SQL from eval/results/harvest.json (h17). Sales revenue over every order status; sold means delivered (eval/README.md).

question: Which seller has sold the most items? Give the seller_id and the number of items sold.
sql: SELECT oi.seller_id, COUNT(*) AS items_sold FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.order_status = 'delivered' GROUP BY oi.seller_id ORDER BY items_sold DESC LIMIT 1;
note: Agent SQL from eval/results/harvest.json (h18). Delivered orders only, as the sales convention requires.

question: Which product category had the highest sales revenue (sum of item prices)? Give the category and the revenue.
sql: SELECT p.product_category_name, SUM(oi.price) AS total_revenue FROM order_items oi JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY p.product_category_name ORDER BY total_revenue DESC LIMIT 1;
note: Agent SQL from eval/results/harvest.json (h19). Sales revenue over every order status; sold means delivered. The Portuguese category name is allowed.

question: What is the average number of installments for credit card payments? Round to two decimals.
sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(payment_installments), 2) AS avg_installments FROM order_payments WHERE payment_type = 'credit_card';
note: Agent SQL from eval/results/harvest.json (h20). Matches the reference.

question: How many products have no category?
sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS no_category_count FROM products WHERE product_category_name IS NULL OR product_category_name = '';
note: Agent SQL from eval/results/harvest.json (h21). Also counts empty strings as no category; same 610 products.

question: How many orders contain items from more than one seller?
sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS orders_with_multiple_sellers FROM ( SELECT order_id FROM order_items GROUP BY order_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT seller_id) > 1 ) t;
note: Agent SQL from eval/results/harvest.json (h22). Matches the reference.

question: What is the total of all payments (payment_value) for orders that contain at least one product from the 'beleza_saude' category, whatever the order status?
sql: SELECT sum(op.payment_value) FROM order_payments op JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = op.order_id JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id WHERE p.product_category_name = 'beleza_saude'
note: Same question as ct05, written with the trap: each payment repeats once per beleza_saude item in the order.

question: Across all orders, what are the total freight value of the items and the total amount paid? Give both numbers.
sql: SELECT sum(oi.freight_value), sum(op.payment_value) FROM order_items oi JOIN order_payments op ON op.order_id = oi.order_id
note: Same question as ct06, written with the trap: freight repeats per payment and payments repeat per item.

question: What is the average latitude of the sellers in the state of Parana (PR)?
sql: SELECT avg(g.geolocation_lat) FROM sellers s JOIN geolocation g ON g.geolocation_zip_code_prefix = s.seller_zip_code_prefix WHERE s.seller_state = 'PR'
note: Each seller counts once per geolocation row of its zip prefix (~53 on average), so prefixes with more rows weigh more. Correct: one coordinate per prefix, then average over sellers.

question: What is the average review score of orders that include at least one product from the 'cama_mesa_banho' category? Round to two decimals.
sql: SELECT round(avg(r.review_score), 2) FROM order_reviews r JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = r.order_id JOIN products p ON p.product_id = i.product_id WHERE p.product_category_name = 'cama_mesa_banho'
note: Same question as ct07, written with the trap: each review repeats once per matching item. Labeled by the SQL, even if the rounded result happens to match.

question: How many orders were there in the first quarter of 2018?
sql: SELECT count(*) FROM orders WHERE order_approved_at >= '2018-01-01' AND order_approved_at < '2018-04-01'
note: Same question as ct15, written with the trap: no date named means purchase date; this uses the approval date.

question: How many orders were delivered to the customer in 2017?
sql: SELECT count(*) FROM orders WHERE order_status = 'delivered' AND order_purchase_timestamp >= '2017-01-01' AND order_purchase_timestamp < '2018-01-01'
note: Same question as ct12, written with the trap: counts delivered orders purchased in 2017, not orders delivered in 2017.

question: In which month of 2017 (as a number from 1 to 12) were the most orders delivered to customers, and how many?
sql: SELECT extract(month FROM order_purchase_timestamp)::int, count(*) FROM orders WHERE order_status = 'delivered' AND order_purchase_timestamp >= '2017-01-01' AND order_purchase_timestamp < '2018-01-01' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 1
note: Same question as ct13, written with the trap: groups by purchase month instead of delivery month.

question: How many orders include at least one product from the 'esporte_lazer' category?
sql: SELECT count(*) FROM order_items i JOIN products p ON p.product_id = i.product_id WHERE p.product_category_name = 'esporte_lazer'
note: Same question as ct09, written with the trap: counts item rows, not orders.

question: What is the average total amount paid per order? Round to two decimals.
sql: SELECT round(avg(payment_value), 2) FROM order_payments
note: Same question as ct08, written with the trap: averages payment rows, and an order can have several.

question: How many orders has the most frequent customer placed?
sql: SELECT customer_id, count(*) FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 1
note: Groups by customer_id, which has one order each, so the top customer always has 1.

question: How many distinct products were sold in 2018?
sql: SELECT count(DISTINCT i.product_id) FROM order_items i JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = i.order_id WHERE o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-01-01' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2019-01-01'
note: Counts products of every order status; sold means delivered.

question: What is the total of all payments (payment_value) made for orders from customers in the state of Rio de Janeiro (RJ), whatever the order status?
sql: SELECT sum(p.payment_value) FROM order_payments p JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = p.order_id JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE c.customer_state = 'RJ'
note: Looks risky (sum after two joins) but each payment matches one order and one customer: no fan-out. customer_id is only the join key.

question: How many distinct sellers have at least one item in an order placed by a customer in the state of Rio de Janeiro (RJ)?
sql: SELECT count(DISTINCT i.seller_id) FROM order_items i JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = i.order_id JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE c.customer_state = 'RJ'
note: Looks risky (three joins) but counts DISTINCT seller_id. Orders, not sales: every status counts.

question: What was the revenue in 2017?
sql: SELECT sum(p.payment_value) FROM order_payments p JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = p.order_id WHERE o.order_status = 'delivered' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2017-01-01' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2018-01-01'
note: Revenue without a measure is ambiguous (item prices, prices plus freight, or payments; eval/README.md); the SQL picked payments without asking.

question: What is the most popular product category?
sql: SELECT p.product_category_name, count(*) FROM order_items i JOIN products p ON p.product_id = i.product_id GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 1
note: 'Popular' could mean items, orders, revenue or reviews; the SQL picked items without asking.

question: Which state has the best customers?
sql: SELECT c.customer_state, count(*) FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 1
note: 'Best' could mean most orders, most spending or best reviews; the SQL picked most orders without asking. cd18 is the dev variant.

question: How many people visited the Olist website in 2017?
sql: SELECT count(DISTINCT c.customer_unique_id) FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2017-01-01' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2018-01-01'
note: The schema has no web traffic; buyers are not visitors.

question: What is the product return rate?
sql: SELECT round(count(*) FILTER (WHERE order_status = 'canceled')::numeric / count(*), 4) FROM orders
note: The schema has no returns; canceled orders are not returns.
